dedupe_keys.name: usgs modeled conterminous united states crop cover datasets 2000 2013 250 m

description: This U.S. Geological Survey data release gives yearly crop cover maps for the conterminous United States from 2000 to 2013 at 250 m, built to extend the NASS Cropland Data Layer (available from 2008) back to 2000. The DataCite record says a classification tree crop model was trained on more than 11 million crop samples, scored over 90 percent on a withheld test set, and was checked against 2008 to 2013 Cropland Data Layers downscaled to 250 m, with a bias toward the "other" class at the edges of large patches and in small scattered patches. It was published on 17 August 2016 by Aaron Friesz, Bruce Wylie and Daniel Howard on ScienceBase, downloadable and free (USGS data; the licence and file sizes are not stated on the pages read). Coverage is national for the lower 48 states. For simulation it gives a consistent crop cover time series to track agricultural exposure to drought and floods before 2008, and to build crop-specific water and fertilizer demand histories. Related catalogue records include the USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer and the Corn-Soy Data Layer.
